items.followUp: Convert 72 km h⁻¹ into m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: Shows conversion of kilometres to metres and hours to seconds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using 1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s in the conversion.

rubric.why: Confirms the converted speed in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 55.56 m s⁻¹ (or an equivalent rounded value).

modelAnswer: Given: speed = 200 km h⁻¹
1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s

rubric.why: The definition identifies the rise in temperature and its connection to greenhouse gases.
rubric.description: Meaning and cause of global warming
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Earth's average temperature is rising and 1 mark for linking the rise to greenhouse gases.

modelAnswer: Global warming is the gradual rise in the average temperature of the Earth due to an increase in greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

items.followUp: What is the moment of a couple?

rubric.why: These are the defining features of the two forces forming a couple.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a couple consists of two equal and opposite parallel forces whose lines of action are different.

rubric.why: A couple produces a turning effect on a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the couple turns or tends to rotate the body.

modelAnswer: A couple consists of two equal and opposite parallel forces acting along different lines of action on a body.
The couple produces a turning effect or rotation of the body.

items.followUp: Define the center of mass of a body.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the point through which the body's weight acts.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that it is the point through which the whole weight of a body acts; award 1 mark for identifying it as a point through which the body's weight acts.

modelAnswer: The center of gravity of a body is the point through which the whole weight of the body acts.

items.followUp: Differentiate between stable equilibrium and unstable equilibrium.

rubric.why: A stable body returns to its original position after a small displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that after a slight displacement the body returns to its original position.

rubric.why: A body in neutral equilibrium remains in its new position after displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that after displacement the body remains in its new position.

modelAnswer: In stable equilibrium, a body returns to its original position when slightly displaced.
In neutral equilibrium, a body remains in its new position when displaced.

items.followUp: Derive the equation for kinetic energy of a body.

rubric.why: The force that must be overcome to raise the body is its weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the force against which work is done as the weight mg.

rubric.why: The work done in raising the body equals its gained potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using work = force × height and obtaining gravitational potential energy mgh.

modelAnswer: To raise a body of mass m through a height h, work is done against its weight.
Weight of the body, F = mg
Work done, W = F × h = mgh
This work is stored as potential energy, so PE = mgh

rubric.why: The joule definition specifies a force of one newton.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force is 1 N.

rubric.why: The displacement must be one metre in the direction of the applied force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying a displacement of 1 m in the force's direction or stating 1 J = 1 N m.

modelAnswer: One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N displaces a body by 1 m in the direction of the force.
1 J = 1 N m

items.followUp: Show that the buoyant force on a body immersed in a liquid is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid.

rubric.why: The difference in pressure between the lower and upper surfaces depends on their vertical separation h.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for establishing that the pressure difference between the lower and upper surfaces is ρgh.

rubric.why: The resultant upward force is the pressure difference multiplied by the area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for expressing the upthrust as the pressure difference times area A.

rubric.why: The displaced volume of the body is its cross-sectional area multiplied by its height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using V = Ah.

rubric.why: Substituting V = Ah gives the required result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining upthrust = ρgV.

modelAnswer: Consider a body of height h and cross-sectional area A immersed in a liquid of density ρ.
Let P₁ and P₂ be the pressures on its upper and lower surfaces, respectively.
Pressure difference, P₂ − P₁ = ρgh
Upthrust, F = (P₂ − P₁)A = ρghA
Volume of displaced liquid, V = Ah
Therefore, upthrust of liquid, F = ρgV
